newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Baloise shares drop as trading resumes.
newsitem.headline: Baloise shares drop as trading resumes.

text.p: Shares in Baloise Insurance Group fell when trading resumed after a suspension due to the company's announcement that it planned a share split and a capital payout rather than a dividend on 1996 results.
Baloise registered shares resumed trading at 65 Swiss francs below Monday's close of 2,875.
They continued to fall, dropping a total of 150 francs to 2,725 about 20 minutes after the resumption at 1300 GMT.

Baloise shares were suspended before the start of trade for a news conference, where the life and non-life insurer said it planned a capital repayment in September 1997 of 80 Swiss francs per registered share.
The payout would be instead of a dividend on 1996 results, after a dividend of 47 Swiss francs this year.
Baloise said that after the pay back, it would split its shares at a ratio of two for one and wind up with a nominal value of 10 Swiss francs.
Baloise also said it would withdraw from Italy, France and Spain to concentrate on more profitable core markets and cut 190 Swiss jobs in the next two years.

Baloise's holding company would sell U.S. subsidiary Providence Washington in the course of 1997 and write-off 150 million on the non-life unit, causing a loss of 81 million Swiss francs at the holding level in the financial year 1996/97.
